mcqs.question: Why doesn't the Issue class hardcode which statuses or transitions are valid?
options: Because that logic belongs to Workflow, letting different projects use entirely different status sets and rules without changing the Issue class
Because Issue objects are immutable once created
Because statuses are determined solely by the assignee's role
Because Issue can only ever have two possible statuses
mcqs.explanation: Delegating status/transition rules to Workflow is exactly what lets two projects run different processes on the same Issue class. Issue objects aren't immutable (status changes over time), status validity has nothing to do with assignee role, and there's no fixed two-status limit.

mcqs.question: A second project needs a QA_REVIEW status between IN_PROGRESS and DONE that the first project doesn't have. What does this design require to support that?
options: A code change and deploy adding QA_REVIEW to a shared status enum used by all projects
Inserting new Status and Transition rows scoped to the second project's own Workflow, with no change to Issue or the first project's workflow
Creating an entirely separate Issue subclass for projects that use QA review
It cannot be supported without duplicating the whole Issue tracker per project
mcqs.explanation: Because workflow is data scoped per project, adding a status is a configuration change — new rows in that project's Workflow — with zero impact on Issue's code or other projects' workflows. A shared enum would require a deploy affecting everyone, and neither a new Issue subclass nor a full duplicate system is needed.

mcqs.question: What is the main risk of a global fixed status enum shared across all projects?
options: It makes issues load more slowly than a configurable workflow
It prevents issues from ever being assigned to more than one user
Adding a status or supporting a different process for one project requires a code change affecting every project, and transition rules tend to scatter as if/else logic instead of living in one place
It is incompatible with storing comments on an issue
mcqs.explanation: The real cost is inflexibility and scattered logic: any process change ships as a code deploy touching every tenant, and without a centralized transition table, validity checks tend to spread across the codebase. This has no bearing on load performance, multi-assignment, or comment storage.
